 1:47 pm, November 15, 2026 Utah escapes defeat...barely 
 🏈 Good morning, football fans, especially a good morning to the Utah Utes fans! 
 When we signed off last night,  No. 2 Utah was in a thriller with the No. 23 Arizona Wildcats . Utah kept their season perfect, winning 40-39. Heading into the fourth, Arizona led 28-24, but it didn't last long once the Utes found their rhythm. Utah clawed back with just 5 minutes left in the fourth. 
 Arizona tried to respond with a touchdown and a successful two-point conversion, taking the lead 39-33 with just under 3 minutes remaining. Yet, Utah's quarterback Devon Dampier was electric, finding Creed Whittemore for a seal-the-deal touchdown. The Utes stay perfect. 
 #GoUtes | #RSNB | 📺 @CFBONFOX https://t.co/JgEDiIB0XC
— Utah Football (@Utah_Football) November 15, 2026 
 No. 12 Texas Tech pulled through with a dominant performance, defeating Oklahoma State, 52-27 . Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos had a strong performance, finishing with 263 yards, 12-of-23, and four touchdowns. 
 Second score of the day for Simmons 🔥 📺: ESPN https://t.co/lM0Sfud2IZ
— Texas Tech Football (@TexasTechFB) November 15, 2026 
 Dont worry, football fans, the games aren't over yet. No. 19 Ole Miss takes on Oklahoma today at 1 p.m. ET.  Due to this date change, a reminder: the AP Top 25 rankings will now come out on Monday, Nov. 16, followed by the CFP bracket and rankings on Tuesday, Nov. 17. 
 share with Facebook copy link 4:53 am, November 15, 2026 👋 Signing off for the night
 We're heading out for the night, but there's still plenty of action going on late into the night. Here's what you should keep an eye on:
 Games still going on:
 There are still two ranked games going on into the late night:
 No. 3 Utah leads No. 23 Arizona, 17-14, heading into halftime 
 No. 12 Texas Tech leads No. 25 Oklahoma State in the third, 35-20 
 Lots of CFP implications from today's games 
 The top teams in the CFP shouldn’t shift too much, but expect plenty of shake-ups further down the committee's rankings on Tuesday after another wild Saturday.
 Teams on both sides of the bubble either stayed alive, delivered dominant performances, or saw their playoff hopes fall.
 In case you missed any of them, here are the games from today with major CFP implications:
 Must-know results: 
 No. 9 Indiana knocked off No. 18 Southern California, 27-13 
 No. 6 Texas survived No. 21 LSU, 22-21 
 Florida upset No. 11 Kentucky, 21-14 
 No. 10 BYU dominated Baylor, 28-7 
 No. 13 Wake Forest crushed SMU, 49-7 
 No. 15 Iowa defeated Purdue, 28-7 
 No. 16 Oregon dominated Michigan, 31-7 
 Arkansas took down No. 17 South Carolina, 34-6 
 No. 24 Boise State survived Oregon State, 46-41 
 We'll be back in the morning to see how the rest of the games shake out. Plus, No. 19 Ole Miss and Oklahoma face off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.  
 share with Facebook copy link 4:49 am, November 15, 2026 Texas Tech battling Oklahoma State in Stillwater
 No. 12 Texas Tech is battling it out with No. 25 Oklahoma State at the half, 28-20.  
 The Red Raiders started the night with a 97-yard kick-return TD on the opening kickoff before jumping out to a 21-0 lead in the first quarter, but the Cowboys responded with 20 points of their own to make it a one-score game at halftime.
 Why does this matter?
 Based on last week's CFP rankings, Texas Tech would have been the first team out of the CFP started today. Kentucky — which would have been the last team in — lost to an unranked Florida team earlier.
 No. 12 Texas Tech goes up THREE scores against No. 25 Oklahoma State in Stillwater 😲 https://t.co/ZJKY5buVQl
— ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) November 15, 2026 
 If Texas Tech can keep it rolling and can take down a fellow ranked opponent, the Red Raiders’ playoff hopes should continue to rise.
 share with Facebook copy link 4:34 am, November 15, 2026 Texas RALLIES with clutch final drive
 It was a chaotic night in Death Valley. Six interceptions. Sixteen penalties. Seven sacks. And it all came down to the final drive.
 No. 21 LSU scored a touchdown in each of the first three quarters. No. 6 Texas, meanwhile, could only settle for field goals after its touchdown on the opening drive — until the final drive of the fourth quarter.
 The two teams traded possessions in the fourth quarter, with the Tigers leading the Longhorns 21-16. The Texas defense forced four consecutive punts, giving its offense chance after chance to take the lead.
 After a shanked LSU punt before the two-minute warning, Arch Manning and the Longhorns were set up in excellent field position with three timeouts.
 After crawling down the field, the Longhorns finally found the endzone for the second time, as Manning connected with Raleek Brown on a 4-yard touchdown pass with two seconds left.
 TEXAS TAKES THE LEAD OVER LSU😳 (via ABC) https://t.co/bHX3GWeixf
— On3 (@On3) November 15, 2026 
 And with that, Texas all but cements a CFP berth and remains firmly in the running for the SEC championship game after a Kentucky loss today.
 What an ending.
 Arch Manning was hype after Texas beat LSU in Baton Rouge👀 (via ABC) https://t.co/8TXSLWU7mX
— On3 (@On3) November 15, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 2:55 am, November 15, 2026 97-yard kickoff return! Texas Tech on the board
 No. 25 Oklahoma State won the coin toss at home and decided to let No. 12 Texas Tech start on offense.
 The Red Raiders wasted no time and immediately made it to the end zone. Dodging multiple defenders along the way, Malcolm Williams returned the kickoff 97-yards for a touchdown.
 What a way to start a top 25 matchup.
 Didn't take long. 📺: ESPN https://t.co/TzZimEas1g
— Texas Tech Football (@TexasTechFB) November 15, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 2:41 am, November 15, 2026 Halftime in Death Valley: No. 21 LSU leads No. 6 Texas
 It’s been a back-and-forth matchup between No. 6 Texas and No. 21 LSU — with both touchdowns and interceptions.
 QB Arch Manning and the Longhorns opened the game with a touchdown drive that saw three LSU penalties. The Tigers immediately responded with a 10-yard touchdown pass to WR Jackson Harris. 
 MANNING ON THE MOVE 🏃‍♂️ https://t.co/z3V6EUvpXI
— Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 15, 2026 
 LSU QB Sam Leavitt then threw two interceptions on consecutive possessions, but Texas failed to capitalize. Manning followed suit with an interception of his own. 
 Benefield Picks Off Manning https://t.co/NfiaSM47LL
— LSU Football (@LSUfootball) November 15, 2026 
 The Tigers added one more touchdown before halftime, while the Longhorns added a field goal.
 Lots of football still to go in Death Valley!
 share with Facebook copy link 1:58 am, November 15, 2026 Two close games: Major CFP hopes on the line
 While you’ve probably been watching No. 6 Texas at No. 22 LSU, we have two close games with major College Football Playoff implications brewing. 
 If the CFP started today, the No. 11 and 12 seeds would be Kentucky and Boise State, respectively. Both are on upset watch in home territory right now.
 On the iconic blue field, No. 24 Boise State has a 39-34 lead over Oregon State — however, the Beavers have kept surging back all night long. Teams like New Mexico, Liberty and North Texas should be on high alert for the G6 qualifying spot if Oregon State can pull this off.
 TOUCHDOWNNNN Beavers 👏🔥 @SmvOperator ➡️ @cynai_thomas 📺 @USANetwork https://t.co/6cfygbnUZT
— Oregon State Football (@BeaverFootball) November 15, 2026 
 Florida, meanwhile, is shocking No. 11 Kentucky, leading 21-14 with 9:08 left in the fourth . The Gators have kept the Wildcats on their toes with a safety, plus two successful 2-point conversions. The chaos in the SEC is not stopping tonight. 
 Let Aaron Philo cook 👨‍🍳 93 rush yards and a TD ⤵️ https://t.co/UKEJ2sxv9N
— Florida Gators Football (@GatorsFB) November 15, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 12:37 am, November 15, 2026 Close game watch: Kentucky 7, Florida 2 at the half
 No. 11 Kentucky, fighting for a top spot within the SEC, narrowly leads Florida 7-2 as both teams head into the locker room.
 .@c4era_ TUDDY 🙌 📺 - ESPN https://t.co/7OAP57OvJT
— Kentucky Football (@UKFootball) November 14, 2026 
 The Gators' defense has put pressure on Kentucky's Kenny Minchey, even nabbing a safety, ultimately limiting the Wildcats' quarterback to just over 90 yards of total offense. 
 Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner and head coach Jon Sumrall, a former Kentucky player and assistant coach, have yet to find consistency within their offense tonight, which has been notorious for spooking top-ranked teams this season.
 share with Facebook copy link 11:53 pm, November 14, 2026 Rounding up some afternoon scores
 How is it already time for some night games? 
 Week 11 has flown by with excitement happening all across the afternoon slate. Let's dive into some final scores:
 No. 9 Indiana 27, No. 18 Southern Cal 13 
 Despite Josh Hoover being off the injury report, Indiana went with Grant Wilson -- and boy, are they glad they did.
 The Hoosiers snuck past the Trojans, 27-13, anchored by Wilson's solid stat line: 17-of-27 for 305 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. 
 Charlie Becker DIVES into the end zone to extend the @IndianaFootball lead 💥 Watch on CBS https://t.co/7esRSzECIR
— Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 14, 2026 
 No. 1 Georgia 48, No. 22 Missouri 21 
 The Bulldogs, who opened the game with an interception, dominated the Tigers 48-21 in Athens. Backed by a Nate Fraizer hat trick, Georgia improves to 9-1. 
 No. 16 Oregon 31, Michigan 7 
 Dylan Raiola had himself a game, going 20-of-28 and racking up 341 yards for four touchdowns. 
 On the other hand, Michigan's quarterback room, not so much.
 Tommy Carr, who started 1-of-5 for 8 yards, was replaced by Bryce Underwood early. Underwood, however, wasn't quite what the Wolverines were looking for in relief, finishing 2-of-8 for 26 yards. Neither signal caller had a touchdown.  
 All kinds of room for Dakorien! @RaiolaDylan 🤝 @thereal_kori2x #GoDucks https://t.co/Qh9vDMEkBe
— Oregon Football (@oregonfootball) November 14, 2026 
 No. 5 Notre Dame 41, Boston College 7 
 The Fighting Irish certainly didn't struggle against Boston College, walking away with a 41-7 win over the Eagles.
 Notre Dame running back Jonaz Walton recorded 141 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.
 share with Facebook copy link 11:41 pm, November 14, 2026 Missouri State walks off New Mexico State with a OT pick-six
 Joel. Boamah. 
 In case you missed it, Missouri State's Boamah nabbed a walk-off 88-yard pick-six in overtime against New Mexico State to win 27-21 . 
 JOEL BOAMAH CALLS GAME 📺 ESPN+ @MoStateFootball | #NoLimitsOnUs https://t.co/5yGqztoB4v
— Conference USA (@ConferenceUSA) November 14, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 10:59 pm, November 14, 2026 Close game watch: Indiana 20, Southern Cal 13
 It's the end of the third quarter in Bloomington and all eyes are on Indiana versus Southern Cal. 
 The Hoosiers and Trojans are neck-and-neck entering the fourth quarter in a battle that will likely alter the College Football Playoff race.
 Indiana leads 20-13  anchored by backup quarterback Grant Wilson. Wilson, who earned the start after veteran Josh Hoover was sidelined due to an upper body/arm injury, is 13-of-22 for 230 yards, a touchdown and an interception. 
 The Hoosiers fell five spots after having a bye week, so a loss could tarnish their playoff hopes. 
 ALL TIED UP 🙌 📺 CBS https://t.co/uZXFKa5BXU
— USC Football ✌️ (@uscfb) November 14, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 10:00 pm, November 14, 2026 TO THE HOUSE! Virginia's 100-yard pick-six
 You all have GOT to check this out.
 Virginia's Brandyn Hillman nabbed a 100-yard pick-six -- the longest interception return in program history. The Cavaliers lead Cal 16-7 at the half.
 🤯🤯🤯 @dmv_b3's PICK-6 GOES FOR 100 YARDS‼️ That's the longest interception return in school history. 📺 ACCN https://t.co/uAF94YMGJD
— Virginia Football (@UVAFootball) November 14, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 9:31 pm, November 14, 2026 Some SEC shenanigans
 If there's anything this college football season has taught us, it’s that the unexpected should be expected — especially within the Top 25 and amongst SEC teams.
 No. 8 Tennessee is trailing an unranked Texas A&M team 6-7 heading into the half. If the Volunteers lose, they’ll be bunched within the three-loss team category of teams that could make the committee’s final bracket.
 Meanwhile, in Athens, No. 1 Georgia is routing No. 22 Missouri 21-0 — and the second quarter just started. The Tigers opened things up with an interception, setting up Nate Fraizer for an early score. Fraizer has two touchdowns on nine carries for just over 40 yards.
 Nate Frazier gets in and the Dawgs are up 21 in the first 👀 📺 ABC x @SEC https://t.co/HC6GL3SmK7
— CFP (@CFBPlayoff) November 14, 2026 
 As for No. 3 Alabama, the Crimson Tide struggled against a relentless Vanderbilt defense today, but pulled off a 21-6 win over the Commodores.  
 Tonight, keep an eye on No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU and No. 11 Kentucky versus Florida . Truthfully, nobody really knows how these games could go.
 share with Facebook copy link 8:54 pm, November 14, 2026 Ferris State breaks NCAA DII football record with 41st consecutive win
 It’s been 805 days since Ferris State last lost a game. That means the DII win record is now the Bulldogs'.
 Ferris State routed Roosevelt 63-20 on Saturday , its 41st consecutive win that sets a DII football record. The Bulldogs led 42-0 and piled up 590 yards, with Marcel Jones running for three of Ferris State's seven rushing touchdowns.
 The Bulldogs haven't lost since Aug. 31, 2024. The streak has included nine consecutive wins in the playoff and two national titles. The program also has won the DII national title four times in the last five seasons.
 It's not the only long streak, either. Ferris State's 35 consecutive home wins at Top Taggart Field is also a DII record.
 Jake Price punches in HIS first of the day! Ferris State goes up 56-14 with a 4-yard rush by Jake Price💨 📺: https://t.co/YOfsnNXgLj @GLIAC | @FerrisFootball #GLIAC | Aug 27 - Nov 14 | Live on FloCollege https://t.co/iNE9Om3UMT
— FloCollege | Football (@FloCollegeFB) November 14, 2026 
 The record-breaking win is just the latest blowout win for the Bulldogs. Last week, Fresno State  tied Grand Valley State’s 40-game DII win streak (set 2005-07)  after an 80-0 win over Wayne State (MI).

 share with Facebook copy link 8:32 pm, November 14, 2026 An afternoon scores update
 The noon slate is coming to a close, so let’s catch up on today’s action so far.
 No. 20 Ohio State survived Northwestern 28-19 despite the Wildcats’ last second six-play, 67-yard touchdown drive as the clock hit zero.
 No. 7 Miami outlasted Duke, coming up with a 36-25 victory. Darian Mensah went 30-of-41 for 382 yards and one touchdown.
 Tied 20-20 with two minutes to go, Maryland and Wisconsin nearly found themselves in overtime, but the Terps’ 30-yard field goal with 32 seconds left on the clock sealed the Maryland win. 
 No. 13 Wake Forest stomped out SMU 49-7 with over 500 yards of Demon Deacon offense.
 No. 3 Alabama leads Vanderbilt 21-6 with five minutes to go in the fourth quarter.
 As the afternoon window gets going, we'll be here to keep you updated on everything you need to know. 
 No. 8 Tennessee at Texas A&M as well as No. 9 Indiana versus No. 18 Southern Cal are underway, with No. 1 Georgia versus No. 22 Missouri slated to begin shortly.
